text:
maya: heads up — during a scheduled canary restore I hit KMS decryption failures for a small subset of DB snapshots. triage time.
maya: quick summary: 3 objects under s3://redwood-backups/db-prod/2026-03-21/ exposed decrypt errors when the restore job ran. restore script bails with `KMS:AccessDeniedException` on decrypt.
samir: do we have CloudTrail events for the Decrypt API calls? who owns the uploader SA right now? any recent RBAC changes?
maya: owner looks like backup-uploader-sa (k8s service account) — there was a terraform RBAC refactor yesterday that touched backup iam binding and a PR touching kms grants. suspect mismatch.
leo: can you paste head-object / metadata for one of the failing objects? sometimes header metadata (cipher headers) misalign with key id.
\
maya: pasted below — note the metadata fields:

```
$ aws s3api head-object --bucket redwood-backups --key db-prod/2026-03-21/snap-03.snap
{
  "ContentLength": 234567890,
  "Metadata": {
    "x-amz-meta-cipher-version": "v2",
    "x-amz-meta-kms-cmk-id": "arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111122223333:key/abcd-ef01-2345",
    "x-amz-meta-backup-agent": "uploader-v3"
  }
}
```

maya: restore logs show:

```
ERROR: decrypt failed for snapshot snap-03.snap: KMS AccessDeniedException: User: arn:aws:sts::111122223333:assumed-role/backup-uploader/xyz is not authorized to perform: kms:Decrypt on resource arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111122223333:key/abcd-ef01-2345
```
alex: hmm — the CMK id in metadata looks right. If the SA lost `kms:Decrypt` in the refactor, CloudTrail should show `Decrypt` calls failing. also check if we accidentally swapped to a different CMK (rotation script?)
samir: checking CloudTrail now — I see a spike of `Decrypt` failures at 2026-03-21T02:34Z for principal `backup-uploader`. matching request IDs attached. I also see a terraform PR (PR#4821) that changed the `backup-uploader` role trust and removed a conditional grant.
oncall: tagging inc-ops: we should treat this as a partial-availability incident for canary restores. low-sev but we need a rollback plan.
maya: proposed immediate mitigation:
1) reapply a targeted kms:Decrypt grant to `backup-uploader` for CMK `abcd-ef01-2345` (short-lived grant) using a KMS grant or IAM policy.
2) run a canary decrypt/restore for the 3 affected snapshots.
3) add detection: CloudWatch metric + alert on repeated KMS AccessDenied for backup principal.
4) audit object metadata for `x-amz-meta-kms-cmk-id` inconsistencies and run integrity scan across last 7 days.

samir: +1. prefer KMS Grant (CreateGrant) with a TTL vs re-editing long-lived IAM policies while we investigate terraform drift.

leo: for the longer term we need:
- an automation that validates snapshot metadata vs CMK key policy (CI job)
- require a test decrypt after any RBAC/Terraform change to backup-related roles
- ensure CloudTrail insights alert for Decrypt failures crosses a threshold

alex: quick rollback option: revert PR#4821 which removed the conditional grant. that gets us immediate restore ability while we craft a safer policy.
maya: doing a targeted CreateGrant now (will attach grant id here once applied). small note: some snapshots include `x-amz-meta-cipher-version: v1` and v2. need to confirm runtime supports both — if not, that explains some failures.
encops-bot: Alert created: KMS-Decrypt-Failures-BackupUploader (severity: medium). runbook: /docs/encops/backup-kms-restore.md
maya: grant applied (grantId: g-0a1b2c3d). re-run canary restore for snap-03.snap — decrypt now passes locally, restore completed to staging.
samir: great. next steps assigned:
- samir: revert PR#4821 (or reintroduce grant) — target: 1 hour
- leo: write CI check to validate snapshot metadata vs CMK existence — target: EOD
- alex: add terraform guardrail to prevent removal of backup KMS grants without manual review — target: next sprint
- maya: run full scan for 7-day window and produce list of affected objects — target: 4 hours

oncall: I'll update the incident board and send a short blameless summary to leadership after the scan.
leo: one more ask — can we add EncryptionContext check to grants (e.g., key condition `EncryptionContext: { "purpose": "backup" }`) so accidental grants for other uses don't open us up? saves narrow-scopes.
samir: yes, use grant with `Constraints` on encryption context and restrict via IAM conditions where supported. also consider using asymmetric/ephemeral keys for uploader agent if we want stronger forward secrecy.
maya: logging note: we were missing a map from snapshot -> CMK in our internal metadata store for some older uploads; adding that to migration backlog.
alex: cool. create a postmortem doc after the scan with timeline + root cause (terraform RBAC refactor removed grant). include remediation: CI checks + tighter grants + runbook updates.
maya: thanks all. will paste the final affected list and incident summary into #postmortems once complete. :thumbsup:
